CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Maintain our current proportionate retaliation on the ~$34B List 1 goods and do not escalate into a full-scale response against the proposed $200B list, while keeping the door firmly open to a negotiated off-ramp. We should signal readiness to return to the table and use the ZTE settlement as evidence that managed de-escalation is possible, without making pre-emptive concessions on structural IP or technology-transfer demands. The goal is to contain the dispute before it triggers the full tariff cascade that would directly pressure our currency, capital account, and export hubs.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat is real and rising but not yet existential. On the threat side: US 25% tariffs on ~$34B of our goods took effect July 6 and we matched them the same day (timeline 2018-07-06); the US published a proposed ~$200B/10% List 3 on July 10 whose comment process is still running (timeline 2018-07-10); firm-level targeting was demonstrated by the April ZTE denial order, lifted only on July 13 after we paid a ~$1.4B penalty and restructured management (Reuters/NYT 2018-07-13). The CNY has fallen ~6-7% since mid-April to ~6.7/USD, its sharpest slide since 2015, and analysts flag capital-flight risk were we to weaponize depreciation (CNBC 07-03; MERICS Q2). This is squarely the CHN +0.5 high anchor: major export sectors hit, FX pressure, firm-level targeting. Yet it is not existential: Q2 GDP was 6.7%, within the 6.5-7% target and above the 6.4% floor needed for 2020 doubling goals; exports still grew 12.3% YoY in Q2 with tariff effects not yet registering (CNBC 07-16; MERICS); reserves are ~$3.1T and adequate (US Treasury Apr 2018). On the action side, escalating further is self-defeating: we already import far less from the US than we export, so tariff-retaliation tools are nearly exhausted, and matching against the $200B list risks a full cascade that hits our own exports, currency and financial stability. Given a real but manageable threat and limited further escalation leverage, the disciplined stance is negotiate/hold — proportionate defense now, negotiated containment rather than maximal escalation.
key_factors: US List 1 25% tariff effective July 6 ~$34B; China matched; List 3 $200B/10% proposed July 10
CNY fell ~6-7% since mid-April to ~6.7/USD with capital-flight risk if depreciated further
China Q2 GDP 6.7% within target; exports +12.3% YoY; tariff impact not yet in data
ZTE ban lifted July 13 after ~$1.4B penalty — a usable de-escalation precedent
China's tariff-retaliation capacity limited (imports << exports); further escalation self-hurting
